initiatives.- Ownership of marketing activities from planning and execution through performance evaluation and optimization.- A dynamic, international environment where collaboration, initiative, and commercial creativity are valued.Keys to Success:Education- A degree in Life Sciences, Molecular Biology, Biotechnology, Marketing, Business, or a related field is advantageous.Experience- Demonstrated experience in market development, commercial marketing, product marketing, or a comparable customer-facing commercial role.- Experience working closely with sales teams to develop demand, manage multiple priorities and collaborate effectively across functions and countries.- Fluent business English and German are non negotiable; additional relevant European languages are an advantage.- Willingness to travel regularly across the Central Region and spend meaningful time with customers and field teams.Competencies- Commercial acumen: Understands customer needs and identifies opportunities to accelerate market adoption and revenue growth.- Customer focus: Builds strong relationships and translates customer insights into relevant solutions and activities.- Collaboration and jobs.description: Technical University Munich operates the high flux Neutron Source Heinz Maier-Leibnitz (FRM II) located at the scientific campus in Garching, Germany. The group plays a key role in advancing methodological development in neutron imaging worldwide.ANTARES is a versatile imaging instrument using thermal and cold neutrons for a broad range of radiography and tomography applications. NECTAR can switch between thermal- and fast-neutron operation and offers worldwide unique capabilities for fast-neutron imaging, enabling the investigation of large and highly absorbing samples that are difficult to access with conventional neutron or X-ray imaging. The complementary capabilities of ANTARES and NECTAR provide an excellent basis for developing and applying such approaches.You will work across our neutron imaging activities at ANTARES and NECTAR, with a particular focus on fast-neutron imaging and the operation and further development of NECTAR. German language skills are beneficial.Willingness to work in a controlled area in a research reactor environment.Demonstrated ability to conduct independent scientific research and motivation to develop an own scientific research profile.For further information about the position, please contact Robin Woracek, E-Mail: Robin.Woracek@frm2.tum.de .
